context.objective: Document how we carry out European Distribution Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The scanned decisions table uses T+7, T+8, and T+15 timelines. What event defines T in the distribution process?

T is the date the client notifies us at GP Fund Solutions of a distribution, and that notification is what starts the work. As the preparer I open the event that same day: I record T, the entity, the amount, the purpose and the expected payment date, set up the schedule from T+3 through T+15, and open the checklist. T has to match the date on the client's notification. One thing I can't tell you is whether the T+n days are business days or calendar days. That has never been confirmed to me, and the process owner would have to say.
Once you’ve opened the event and checklist, what happens next in the normal distribution process?

Next I draft the investor calculations, working with Fund Accounting. For each investor I prepare the gross distribution amount, any withholding and the net payment amount in the distribution calculation file, check that the investor totals agree with the approved fund-level distribution, and share the draft with the client by T+3. The client sends comments by T+4. The reviewer and I work through those comments, update the calculations and allocations, and prepare the distribution notices by T+5. We rerun the affected comparison checks and keep each version. I can't review my own work, so every checklist section needs the reviewer's initials as well as mine.
What determines the withholding amount for each investor?

That isn't worked out in this process. The waterfall, tax and withholding calculations are done in a separate process, and I take the gross amount, any withholding, the net amount paid and the investor list from the approved calculation file that comes out of it. The fund's governing terms, meaning the current limited partnership agreement and any side letters, control the distribution amounts and the allocation rules. If the terms or amounts I've been given don't agree, I refer it back to that calculation process and to the client rather than fix it myself.
What do you compare the investor totals against to decide they agree with the approved fund-level distribution?

Against the approved distribution terms and amounts for the fund. The investor amounts added together have to equal the approved fund-level amount. I do that check on the draft at T+3 and again on the final calculation at T+5, the reviewer reviews it, and the calculation record is what we keep. If it doesn't agree I record the exception, and the item doesn't move forward until the issue is resolved or an authorised decision is documented.
What marks the distribution work as finished, including any required handoff or downstream use?

The event is finished when the checklist and all the required records are complete and filed in the digital binder: the calculation, the client's approval, the notices, the screening and CDD records, the payment and payment-completion records and the follow-up records, with the reviewer's initials and mine on the checklist. Before that the client has to have approved the notices in writing at T+7, the notices go out at T+8, and the cleared payments are released at T+15. Anything still open, like a CDD-blocked investor or a returned payment, is not marked closed. It is recorded and tracked separately, and we keep reporting payment status and returned payments to the client from one day after the due date until each item is resolved. The records in the binder are then used for quarterly and entity reporting. I don't know who gives the final sign-off or how long the records have to be kept. Neither is specified, and the system owner or a process expert would have to confirm the retention period.
What can go wrong in distribution execution, and what happens as a result?
This capture still has open sections. 16 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.
